reviewScope: Black Whale vessel, spatial, access, operational, structural and scale evidence only

pass1.method: Full-page visual sweep of all 18 ordered pages

pass2.method: Full-resolution verification of retained diagrams, corridors, room thresholds, intercoms and guard deployment panels

retainedPanels.subject: Tier 1 royal residential block diagram
retainedPanels.visualDescription: An axonometric block diagram shows a central cluster of numbered royal rooms, perimeter circulation, access arrows, a broad common approach and a small inset plan for one suite.
modelingPermissions: Use the numbered-room cluster and perimeter circulation as a relative topology reference
Record visible access arrows and common approach zones
modelingProhibitions: Do not assume hidden walls or vertical stacking
Do not convert perspective spacing into exact distances

retainedPanels.subject: Royal corridor outside Room 1001
retainedPanels.visualDescription: A wide decorated corridor includes a clearly mounted 1001 room plaque, repeated wall bays, a large doorway and circulation space sufficient for several guards.
modelingPermissions: Use 1001 as a verified doorway label
Use the corridor as a Tier 1 royal-suite circulation type
modelingProhibitions: Do not infer exact corridor width
Do not assume every royal corridor is identical

retainedPanels.subject: Dense guard deployment in a royal room
retainedPanels.visualDescription: A large furnished chamber contains two opposing lines of guards around a central open floor, with multiple doors and wall bays visible around the perimeter.
modelingPermissions: Represent the room as able to hold a dense multi-party guard formation
modelingProhibitions: Do not derive exact occupancy capacity
Do not treat this temporary formation as permanent furniture layout

retainedPanels.subject: Room 1014 threshold and corridor
retainedPanels.visualDescription: A wall-mounted 1014 plaque marks a royal-suite doorway opening directly onto the decorated Tier 1 corridor.
modelingPermissions: Use Room 1014 as a verified corridor-facing suite threshold
modelingProhibitions: Do not infer its exact position from this panel alone

retainedPanels.subject: Royal-suite intercom and monitored doorway
retainedPanels.visualDescription: A wall intercom with screen, keypad and call controls is mounted beside a large suite doorway while a guard stands inside the threshold.
modelingPermissions: Include a fixed video-intercom station beside at least some royal-suite doors
Represent doorway guard posts as an operational state
modelingProhibitions: Do not generalize identical hardware to every door without corroboration

evidence.claim: The numbered royal residences shown in the chapter diagram belong to Tier 1.
evidence.modelingUse: Anchor the royal residential cluster to Tier 1.

evidence.claim: The royal rooms are arranged as a compact numbered cluster bordered by circulation space rather than as isolated cabins.
evidence.modelingUse: Build a relative adjacency graph, not a metric plan.

evidence.claim: The diagram presents controlled approach paths and perimeter routes around the royal-room block.
evidence.modelingUse: Represent controlled approach and perimeter circulation nodes.

evidence.claim: Royal guards are shown occupying and monitoring the decorated Tier 1 corridor outside the suites.
evidence.modelingUse: Store guard presence as a chapter-state overlay rather than permanent geometry.

evidence.claim: Tier 1 royal circulation uses broad decorated corridors with repeated wall bays, large doors and ceiling coffers.
evidence.modelingUse: Define a verified royal-corridor visual type.

evidence.claim: Room 1001 has a corridor-facing numeric plaque mounted beside its threshold.
evidence.modelingUse: Register Room 1001 as a verified labeled threshold.

evidence.claim: Room 1001 opens directly onto the royal corridor and can be approached by multiple guards simultaneously.
evidence.modelingUse: Connect Room 1001 to the Tier 1 royal corridor node.

evidence.claim: Royal suites contain large furnished reception or meeting areas capable of holding several guards and occupants.
evidence.modelingUse: Permit a large reception-space programme without fixing dimensions.

evidence.claim: A royal room includes a rectangular table with multiple chairs within a formally finished interior.
evidence.modelingUse: Record a meeting-table furniture state for the shown room only.

evidence.claim: One royal chamber can hold two opposing lines of guards while retaining a central open circulation strip.
evidence.modelingUse: Constrain the room to a large multi-party occupancy class.

evidence.claim: The same chamber shows multiple perimeter doorways or wall openings supporting more than one circulation connection.
evidence.modelingUse: Allow multiple room thresholds, with exact destinations unresolved.

evidence.claim: Room 1014 has a numeric plaque beside a corridor-facing doorway.
evidence.modelingUse: Register Room 1014 as a verified labeled threshold.

evidence.claim: A fixed video intercom with screen and keypad is installed beside a royal-suite doorway.
evidence.modelingUse: Add a royal-suite door communications and visitor-screening system.

evidence.claim: A guard can be stationed immediately inside the suite doorway while communicating through the wall unit.
evidence.modelingUse: Store an interior threshold guard-post state.

evidence.claim: Characters explicitly discuss watching a suite entrance continuously from the adjacent corridor.
evidence.modelingUse: Register line-of-sight entrance surveillance as an operational use of the corridor.

contradictionsAndQuarantines.subject: Diagram proportions
contradictionsAndQuarantines.rule: The Chapter 363 axonometric diagram establishes relative topology and numbering but not metric dimensions or exact wall geometry.

contradictionsAndQuarantines.subject: Room identity in guard-formation panels
contradictionsAndQuarantines.rule: Do not assign the large guard-filled chamber to a specific room number unless the same sequence or later evidence explicitly confirms it.

unresolvedQuestions: Which exact numbered rooms occupy every position in the axonometric block where labels are partially obscured?
Which diagram arrows indicate public approach, staff access, emergency routing or merely narrative movement?
Are all royal-suite intercoms the same model or is the shown unit room-specific?

excludedMaterial.reason: Excluded panels do not independently establish Black Whale geometry, location hierarchy, access, route, operational system, scale cue or durable chapter-state evidence.
